newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestine International Bank to open Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Palestine International Bank to open Saturday.

text.p: The Palestine International Bank (PIB) is to open formally for business on Saturday, becoming the sixth Palestinian-owned bank to operate in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, bank officials said on Friday.

"With Palestine International Bank's high tech and progressive banking policies, PIB is already becoming known as 'The Gateway to Palestine - where Palestine meets the world'," a statement issued by the bank said.
It said it would offer "a 24-hour-per-day, seven-day-a-week service which you can access by using a touch telephone or via the Internet, from the comfort of home or office".
The bank, based in the West Bank town of al-Bireh, was founded in 1996 by wealthy Palestinians and Arabs from the oil-rich Gulf states with an authorised capital of $20 million.

The Palestinian Monetary Authority (PMA), which acts as a central bank for the Palestinian Authority set up under a framework 1993 peace deal with Israel, said in January there were 17 banks operating 71 branches in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. It said bank deposits in 1996 reached $1.722 billion.
PIB said its services would include issuing travellers cheques, credit cards, ATM machines, safe deposit boxes and a self-service cheque book centre.
